SERVICE.detail: The guide's account of who must be served is false against EXP104's own printed page, which is delivered in this packet as pages 7 and 8. It states: 'The service list is EXP104's fifteen numbered boxes. Three of them are marked (Required) on the form itself and already carry their addresses printed: the MN Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, the Office of the MN Attorney General, and the MN Department of Human Services / Office of Inspector General. The rest are checked and completed only where they relate to your case.' I read every box on the delivered page by x-position and y-band and mapped each printed box number to the marker printed beneath it. SIX boxes are marked (Required), not three: box 1 MN Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, box 2 Office of the MN Attorney General, box 3 MN Dept. of Corrections, box 4 ______ County Attorney's Office, box 5 ______ County Dept. of Corrections (Probation), box 6 ______ County Sheriff's Office. The six boxes marked '(check box & use if related to your case)' are 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12. So the third agency the guide names as Required - MN Department of Human Services / Office of Inspector General - is box 9, and box 9 is one of the CONDITIONAL boxes; and the guide's sentence 'The rest are checked and completed only where they relate to your case' tells the participant that boxes 3, 4, 5 and 6 are optional when the form marks all four (Required). Box 4 is the County Attorney's Office, which the guide's own disclosure table elsewhere calls 'the prosecuting authority the committed record requires you to serve'. A participant following this paragraph would treat service on the prosecuting authority, the county probation department and the county sheriff as discretionary.

crossChecks.NEAR_CLONE_MEASUREMENT: Raised as asked, with the page-level measurement, and bounded by what this lane may read. I hold no claim on il-seal-2yr-set or il-seal-3yr-set and did not open their artifacts, so this is measured from my own family's 13 pages plus MASTER_QUEUE.json, which is a central record I may read. EIGHT Illinois families bind the identical four official forms with the identical four-component shape: il-exp-pardon-set, il-exp-precompletion-set, il-exp-qualprob-set, il-exp-supervision-set, il-seal-2yr-set, il-seal-3yr-set, il-seal-edu-set and il-seal-nonconv-set. Illinois publishes ONE statewide EXP-AD set that serves both expungement and sealing, so near-identity between these families is structural rather than a build error - the route is expressed by which boxes are ticked, not by a different form. The page-level measurement on my family: of 13 canonical pages, exactly FOUR carry route-distinguishing ink - page 1 (item 1 Yes), page 2 (outcome code QP), page 3 (Section 8 tick), page 4 (item 12 No) - and the other NINE carry only caption and participant data that would be identical for any sibling with the same participant. Pages 5, 11 and 12 carry no ink at all. So 9 of 13 pages of this family are, by construction, not distinguishable from a sibling's. The question worth raising is NOT the seal-2yr/seal-3yr pair I was pointed at but a closer one: il-exp-qualprob-set and il-exp-supervision-set share the same route-key wording ('expungement-after-eligible-supervision-or-qualified-probation'), the same four forms and the same item 1 Yes / item 12 No answers, and appear to differ only in WHICH Section 3-11 box is ticked and in a two-letter outcome code - the form's legend prints 'S Supervision Successfully Completed' immediately beside 'QP Qualified Probation Successfully Completed' on the same line of page 2. One tick position and two letters is the whole difference between two commercially distinct routes. That is correct as built here - I verified this family ticks Section 8 and writes QP - but it is a thin margin, and a reader of the two packets side by side should confirm the sibling ticks a different box.
